summary: Teodor Iordănescu was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Bucharest (~1892–1897) and at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1901–1903) under Richard Pischel, Richard Schmidt, and Eugen Hultzsch.

Ter Ellingson is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Concordia College (1966), the University of Chicago (1970), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1979), later serving as a music professor at the University of Washington (1981–2016).
Terence Dukes worked in Buddhist studies. He founded Kongoryuji Temple in 1978, where he held a teaching post.

Terese Tse Bartholomew specializes in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Sinology. She earned an M.A. at UCLA and served at the Asian Art Museum, notably as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art (attested 2001–2003).
Terry Kleeman is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia (~1979–1982) and held a post as professor at the University of Colorado Boulder (~1998).
Tertön Sogyal studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He was a teacher of the 13th Dalai Lama.

Teruji Ishizu was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1926). His posts included president of Tohoku University (1963–1966), president of Miyagi University of Education (1965), and professor at Keio and Komazawa universities (1966).

Tessa J. Bartholomeusz worked in religious and Buddhist studies, earning degrees from Florida State University and the University of Virginia. She taught at the University of Virginia, Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis (~1991–2001), and Florida State University (1993).
Tessa Verney Wheeler was a scholar in the field of history and archaeology. She studied at Addey and Stanhope School (1905–1911) and University College London (1911–1914).

Tetsuei Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1925–1931). He held professorships at Taisho University and Gifu Kyoritsu University (attested 1972), and became professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (~1971–1982).
Tetsuhiko Shibata is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Taisho University under Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

Tetsujiro Inoue specialized in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Heidelberg, Leipzig, and Berlin, and held posts as professor at the University of Tokyo (from 1890), Toyo University (1923), and president of Daito Bunka University (1925).

Tetsuo Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda and Komazawa universities. He held multiple academic posts, including professor and president of Komazawa University (2002–2006) and president of Tohoku Fukushi University (2015–2019).

Tetsuro Noguchi worked in Sinology, history and archaeology, and religious studies. He held posts at Yokohama National University (~1967–1974), the University of Tsukuba (~1974–1996), and J. F. Oberlin University (~1996–2003).

Tetsuro Watsuji was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Martin Heidegger, and served as professor of ethics at Kyoto University (1925–1949) and chair in ethics at the University of Tokyo (1934–1949).

Tetsuzo Tanikawa specialized in philosophy and Japanology. After studying at Kyoto University (~1919–1922), he held posts at Doshisha University (~1928–1938) and as professor at Hosei University (~1938–1965).

Teun Goudriaan was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Jan Gonda. He served at Utrecht University, where he is attested as a committee member (1989) and professor emeritus (2000).
Thanissaro Bhikkhu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oberlin College (~1967–1971) and under Ajahn Fuang Jotiko (~1976–1986). He founded Metta Forest Monastery and became its abbot in 1993.
Thanon Chitkament is a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under guides Vishwas D. Gogte and P. S. Joshi (attested 2021).

Thatchathon Attarung is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies pursuing a Ph.D. at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (2024–2026). In 2024, he served as secretary to the dean's office there and as associate editor for the Journal of Applied Humanities Studies.
